dataImpact: No seeded entitlement, legacy IPN event, or bot row was deleted. All six legitimate-user/system non-BASIC rows were retained but revoked because expires_at_ms was null. Six synthetic valid owner rows matched users and received memberships, while the pseudo-owner system row received none. The separately labeled orphan negative-control row received no workspace/membership. Two session-backed user workspaces were provisioned and both bots were assigned. The signed-finished event establishes a historically recorded callback but not a currently active subscription.
migrationDesign: The broad revocation is an intentional fail-closed rule in 0016, not a finding that the six payments were invalid. The old schema cannot validate amount/currency against a checkout order, bind an event to an owner/order, or establish subscription duration/expiry. A preservation/recovery path must require an owner-reviewed proof manifest with those fields and verifiable supporting evidence; it must only clear revocation for exact matching rows. No grace period or automatic entitlement restoration was applied.
integrityFix: Migration 0016 now creates legacy workspaces/memberships only when owner_user_id exists in users; personal workspace/bot backfills also require a users row. Session authentication joins user_sessions to users and rejects orphan sessions. The test has consistent primary legacy owners plus an explicitly labeled orphan entitlement/session negative control.
limitations: Pre-0016 rows cannot encode expires_at_ms/current_payment_id, order price/fiat currency, or prior explicit revocation. Valid paid customers with no recoverable order/term evidence may lose access under the current fail-closed migration; business must choose how to handle them. The signed-finished callback metadata cannot by itself establish active rights.
